cards.text: Jeremiah, a priest's son from Anathoth, was just called to be a prophet (Jeremiah 1:1, 5). Now the word of the LORD comes to him again: go proclaim it in the hearing of Jerusalem. And the LORD opens not with a scolding, but with a memory.

cards.question: The LORD remembers Israel's love back in her early days. What does He compare that love to?
Back then, Israel followed the LORD through a land of planted fields.

cards.text: Israel was holy to the LORD, the firstfruits of His harvest. Nobody touches my first batch of the morning either, and I WILL defend it with this mustache.

cards.question: Back in those days, what happened to anyone who tried to devour Israel?

cards.text: Now the LORD calls out to the house of Jacob and all the families of Israel. And then He asks a question that stings.

cards.question: The LORD asks a question about Israel's fathers, who strayed so far from Him. What does He want to know?

answers.text: What fault they found in Him
Why they built so many cities
Where they hid all their gold

cards.question: The LORD says Israel's fathers followed worthless idols and became ___ themselves.
The fathers forgot the One who rescued them. What question did they never ask?

answers.text: Where is the LORD who brought us out of Egypt
Why did we ever leave the land of Egypt
Who will give us a king like the nations

cards.text: That's the LORD who led them through a land of deserts and pits, drought and darkness, where no one travels and no one lives. Your phone's map app looks at that place and just says, "Good luck."
Then the LORD brought them into a fertile land, to eat its fruit and bounty. Friend, I went from the back of a junk drawer to a whole bakery, so I KNOW that upgrade.

cards.question: In the fertile land the LORD brought them into, the people kept His land holy.

cards.text: Not even the priests asked, "Where is the LORD?" The experts in the law no longer knew Him, and the leaders rebelled against Him.

cards.question: And the prophets? They prophesied by ___ and followed useless idols.

cards.text: So the LORD declares it: He will contend with them again. Not a warning. A case.

cards.question: The LORD says His case is only against the people living right then.

cards.text: Now the LORD says to cross over to the coasts of Cyprus, send to Kedar, and look carefully. See if there has ever been anything like this.

cards.question: From Cyprus all the way to Kedar, the LORD asks if any nation has ever done what?
Other nations hold on to their gods, and those aren't gods at all. So what have the LORD's people exchanged their Glory for?
The LORD calls on the heavens to sing for joy over what His people have done.

cards.text: The heavens are told to be shocked and utterly appalled. Then the LORD lays it out plain: His people have committed two evils.

cards.question: The first evil: His people have forsaken the LORD. What does He call Himself there?

cards.text: And the second evil: they dug their own cisterns. That's like canceling your water bill to catch rain in a bucket, and it gets WORSE.

cards.question: The cisterns the LORD's people dug for themselves hold water just fine.

cards.text: Next the LORD asks, "Is Israel a slave? Was he born into slavery?"

cards.question: After asking whether Israel is a slave, what does the LORD ask next?

answers.text: Why he has grown so strong
Why he has gone to war

cards.text: The young lions have roared at him. They have laid waste his land, and his cities lie in ruins.

cards.question: Even after the young lions lay waste Israel's land, his cities are still full of people.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "The men of Memphis and Tahpanhes have shaved the crown of your head." Friend, my hands are a MUSTACHE. I don't even like hearing the word shaved.

cards.question: Then the LORD asks Israel, "Have you not brought this on yourself by ___ the LORD your God when He led you in the way?"

cards.text: Now the LORD asks what they'll gain on the way to Egypt and on the way to Assyria, just to go drink somebody else's water. After those leaky cisterns, I can't even watch.

cards.question: On the way to Egypt, they go to drink the waters of the ___.

cards.text: And the Lord GOD of Hosts brings it all home with one last word.

cards.question: What does the Lord GOD of Hosts say will discipline His people?
The LORD tells His people to consider how evil and bitter it is to forsake Him and have no fear of Him.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 14 quotes "Have you not brought this on yourself by ___ the LORD your God when He led you in the way?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: "was just called to be a prophet" adds a time the text doesn't give. Neither Jeremiah 1 nor 2:1 says how long after his call this word came.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: "Now the LORD calls out to the house of Jacob" says the LORD gives the call. In 2:4 the prophet says "Hear the word of the LORD," and the LORD's words begin in 2:5 with "This is what the LORD says." The card gets the speaker wrong.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: "The fathers forgot the One who rescued them" uses a word the text doesn't. Jeremiah 2:6 says they "did not ask" where the LORD is. It never says they forgot.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "Not a warning. A case." states something the text doesn't. Jeremiah 2:9 says the LORD will contend and bring a case. It never says this is not a warning.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The card tells 2:12 (the heavens told to be shocked and utterly appalled) and 2:13, but it cites only Jeremiah 2:13. It should cite Jeremiah 2:12-13.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "and it gets WORSE" is the setup for card 8, a true-or-false asking whether the cisterns hold water just fine. The line rules out True before the baker answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The men of Memphis and Tahpanhes show up for the first time with no word on who they are. Both are Egyptian cities, which also matters for the trip to Egypt in 2:18.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
